<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S4.SS2" title="In 4 Experimental Settings ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">4.2 </span>Comparison Systems</span></a>

<article class="ltx_document">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Deniz Qian
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>Courant Institute School of Mathematics, Computing, and Data Science, New York University
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Correspondence to: </span><a href="mailto:dq2024@nyu.edu">dq2024@nyu.edu</a>
</span></span></span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Hung-Ting Chen
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>Courant Institute School of Mathematics, Computing, and Data Science, New York University
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Correspondence to: </span><a href="mailto:hc3337@nyu.edu">hc3337@nyu.edu</a>
</span></span></span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Eunsol Choi
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>Courant Institute School of Mathematics, Computing, and Data Science, New York University
</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Comprehensively retrieving diverse documents is crucial to address queries that admit a wide range of valid answers. We introduce retrieve-verify-retrieve (RVR), a multi-round retrieval framework designed to maximize answer coverage. Initially, a retriever takes the original query and returns a candidate document set, followed by a verifier that identifies a high-quality subset. For subsequent rounds, the query is augmented with previously verified documents to uncover answers that are not yet covered in previous rounds. RVR is effective even with off-the-shelf retrievers, and fine-tuning retrievers for our inference procedure brings further gains. Our method outperforms baselines, including agentic search approaches, achieving at least 10% relative and 3% absolute gain in complete recall percentage on a multi-answer retrieval dataset (QAMPARI). We also see consistent gains on two out-of-domain datasets (QUEST and WebQuestionsSP) across different base retrievers. Our work presents a promising iterative approach for comprehensive answer recall leveraging a verifier and adapting retrievers to a new inference scenario.</p>
  
</div>
<div class="ltx_keywords">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_keywords">Keywords: </h6>Machine Learning, ICML
</div><span id="id1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_affiliationnotice"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_type">affiliationnotice: </span>Equal contribution</span></span></span>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Retrieval is a key method to equip large language models (LLMs) with up-to-date, long-tail information. Despite the recent advances in retrieval systems, comprehensively recovering relevant documents remains challenging <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Amouyal et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen and Choi, 2025</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure">
<p id="S1.F1.3" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center ltx_align_center"><span id="S1.F1.3.1" class="ltx_text"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18425v1/intro-figure.svg" id="S1.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/366;" width="476" height="366"></object></span></p>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S1.F1.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Overview of our Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve framework. Each query <math id="S1.F1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> aims to retrieve documents to get multiple answers <math id="S1.F1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(y_{1},y_{2},y_{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(y_{1},y_{2},y_{3})</annotation></semantics></math>. The initial retriever takes a query and returns document sets, and the verifier examines each document, identifying two valid answers <math id="S1.F1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{1},y_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{1},y_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The subsequent retriever takes the query and documents containing identified answers as input, targeting to retrieve complementary answer <math id="S1.F1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In this work, we introduce Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve (RVR), a framework that performs multiple rounds of retrieval, where each round conditions on previously retrieved documents verified by an LLM. At the next iteration, the model receives the concatenation of the query and LLM verified output documents from the previous retrieval search, aiming to search for remaining gold documents. The high-quality subsets from the initial step and the outputs returned by the subsequent retriever are merged as the final output. Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> visualizes our approach.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike traditional retrievers that only take a query as input to retrieve documents, our retriever is trained to explicitly condition on previously retrieved, high-quality documents to target missing ones. This formulation encourages improving coverage over iterations, in contrast to a one-shot ranking task between the original query and documents. Recent agentic approaches <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jin et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Team et al., 2025</a>)</cite> also allows iterative search by interweaving retrieval calls and new query formulation, but they mainly targets multi-hop questions which require a sequence of distinct search queries, not multiple retrieval rounds targeting comprehensive answers for the same query.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Our approach is trained and evaluated on an open-domain, multi-answer QA benchmark QAMPARI <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Amouyal et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. Compared to base fine-tuned retrievers as well as recent agentic search framework <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jin et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Team et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, our approach shows consistent improvements in retrieval performance. Using off-the-shelf retrievers iteratively also showed some gains, but larger gains are achieved by fine-tuning retrievers with our inference setting. We further evaluate on other multi-answer QA benchmarks QUEST  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Malaviya et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and WebQuestionsSP  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yih et al., 2016</a>)</cite>, showing that our approach can generalize. To understand the impact of verifier performance, we provide performance under both our oracle verifier and our verifier. The experimental results show oracle verifier can further significantly boost the performance, showing the headroom of the approach with better verifier models.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">In summary, we present a iterative retrieval framework for comprehensive retrieval. Despite rich studies on agentic search, most approaches focus on improving LLMs that generate new queries based on retrieval output rather than adapting retrievers for new inference scenarios. Our results support fine-tuning retrievers for new inference scenarios can bring further performance gains. We release the code and model at <a href="https://github.com/timchen0618/RVR" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/timchen0618/RVR</a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related Work</h2>

<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Comprehensive Retrieval</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We review prior retrieval datasets with queries that admit a list of answers. QAMPARI <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Amouyal et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and QUEST <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Malaviya et al., 2023</a>)</cite> expect a list of entity answers from Wikipedia; <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhu et al. (2024)</a></cite> introduces FanOutQA, which requires multi-hop reasoning over large numbers of documents to aggregate information about multiple entities;  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Katz et al. (2023)</a></cite> expects all documents mentioning a list of entities given an entity type; <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yih et al. (2016)</a></cite> provide WebQuestionsSP, which annotates questions with SPARQL semantic parses over Freebase for knowledge base question answering;  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen and Choi (2025)</a></cite> expect the candidate document set to cover multiple valid perspectives given a subjective question.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In terms of method, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Min et al. (2021)</a></cite> introduces an autoregressive reranker conditioned on previously selected passages to encourage diversity and cover multiple answers.  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al. (2025a)</a></cite> proposed to generate multiple query embeddings autoregressively to retrieve more comprehensive document sets. In contrast to both, we chose iterative framework, where the output from previous retrieval step is provided as an input to the next retrieval stage, similar to recent agentic approaches.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Iterative &amp; Agentic Retrieval</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Several works have explored performing multiple rounds of retrieval for complex question answering <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2018</a>; <a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Trivedi et al., 2022</a>)</cite>. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qi et al. (2019)</a></cite> introduced iterative query reformulation, generating new retrieval queries from partially read passages. A line of work <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xiong et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Trivedi et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> similarly retrieve evidence iteratively, interweaving with intermediate LLM reasoning steps. A more recent line of works on agentic search systems <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jin et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Team et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al., 2025</a>)</cite> explored using retrievers as a tool, and an LLM agent alternates between reasoning and tool calling until it reaches the final answer.
Concurrent work <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sharifymoghaddam and Lin, 2026</a>)</cite> shows that retrieving more documents at each turn and reranking them can improve answer accuracy. While most agentic approaches use off-the-shelf retrievers, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2026)</a></cite> train retrievers for agentic search by optimizing for both local relevance and global answer correctness in single-answer reasoning tasks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Verifier Based Retrieval</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recent work has incorporated verification into retrieval pipelines. Chain-of-Verification (CoVe) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dhuliawala et al., 2024</a>)</cite> has an LLM draft an answer, plan verification questions, retrieve supporting evidence, and revise, reducing hallucinations. Self-RAG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Asai et al., 2024</a>)</cite> integrates retrieval, generation, and critique via self-reflection signals. In these approaches, verification operates <em id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">after</em> retrieval or generation, serving primarily as a filtering mechanism. In contrast, our framework integrates verification <em id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">within</em> the retrieval loop itself: verification determines which retrieved documents are retained and used to condition subsequent retrieval rounds.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Method</h2>

<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Problem Formulation</h3>

<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Multi Answer Retrieval Task</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given a query <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> and a large corpus <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}=\{d_{1},\dots,d_{N}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}=\{d_{1},\dots,d_{N}\}</annotation></semantics></math>,
a retrieval system <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(q,\mathcal{C},K)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(q,\mathcal{C},K)</annotation></semantics></math> should identify a ranked subset of <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> documents
<math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\text{out}}=\{d_{1},\dots,d_{K}\}\subset\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>⊂</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\text{out}}=\{d_{1},\dots,d_{K}\}\subset\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math> that contains all answers <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y={y_{1},y_{2},...,y_{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y={y_{1},y_{2},...,y_{M}}</annotation></semantics></math> for the query <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>. A retriever should aim to maximize both <em id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">relevance</em> and <em id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">coverage</em>,
ensuring that the retrieved set reflects the full range of relevant, high-quality information.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Metrics</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We assume a test set, where each query <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> is annotated with a set of <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> distinct gold answer strings <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y={y_{1},y_{2},...,y_{M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y={y_{1},y_{2},...,y_{M}}</annotation></semantics></math>. We judge that document <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> covers answer <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> if the substring occurs in the document. We report the following two metrics related to task performance:</p>
<ul id="S3.I1" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:10px;">
<li id="S3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MRecall@K</span>: a binary score that
equals 1 if all answers or at least <math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> answers in the answer set <math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{y_{1}...y_{M}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{y_{1}...y_{M}\}</annotation></semantics></math> are covered by <math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\text{out}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\text{out}}</annotation></semantics></math>. This metric was introduced in prior work <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Min et al., 2021</a>)</cite> for questions that admit multiple valid answers.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Recall@K</span>: the fraction of answers <math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> that are covered by at least one document in <math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\text{out}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\text{out}}</annotation></semantics></math>. This is a less stringent metric compared to MRecall@K.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<figure id="alg1" class="ltx_float ltx_float_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float"><span id="alg1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm 1</span> </span> Inference procedure for Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve framework.</figcaption><div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<div id="alg1.4" class="ltx_block ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_middle ltx_framed ltx_framed_topbottom" style="width:162.2pt;">
<p id="alg1.4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="alg1.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Input:</span> A input query <math id="alg1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>, corpus <math id="alg1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math>, initial retriever <math id="alg1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, subsequent retriever <math id="alg1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>, a verifier <math id="alg1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
<p id="alg1.4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="alg1.4.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Hyperparameters:</span> verifier budget per turn <math id="alg1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>, max document context budget <math id="alg1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, maximum number of turns <math id="alg1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>, final output set size <math id="alg1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
<p id="alg1.4.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="alg1.4.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Output:</span> A ranked set of documents <math id="alg1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\text{out}}=\{d_{1},\ldots,d_{K}\}\subset\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>⊂</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\text{out}}=\{d_{1},\ldots,d_{K}\}\subset\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math>, sorted by relevance to <math id="alg1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<div id="alg1.5" class="ltx_listing ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center ltx_listing">
<div id="alg1.l1" class="ltx_listingline">

</div>

                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">2:</span></span>
                
                
              <span id="alg1.l2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><math id="alg1.l2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}\leftarrow f_{i}(q,\mathcal{C},K)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">D</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">i</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em" stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">f</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">q</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathsize="0.900em">𝒞</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">K</mi><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}\leftarrow f_{i}(q,\mathcal{C},K)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="alg1.l2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l3" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">3:</span></span>
                
                
              <span id="alg1.l3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><span id="alg1.l3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">for</span><span id="alg1.l3.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><math id="alg1.l3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in\{1,\ldots,T\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">t</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em" mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">T</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in\{1,\ldots,T\}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="alg1.l3.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><span id="alg1.l3.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">while</span><span id="alg1.l3.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><math id="alg1.l3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|D_{\text{out}}|&lt;K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em" stretchy="true">|</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">D</mi><mtext mathsize="0.900em">out</mtext></msub><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">&lt;</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|D_{\text{out}}|&lt;K</annotation></semantics></math><span id="alg1.l3.9" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> </span><span id="alg1.l3.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">do</span><span id="alg1.l3.11" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">


</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l4" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">4:</span></span>

<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Iterative Retrieval Framework</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ Metrics ‣ 3.1 Problem Formulation ‣ 3 Method ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> describes our iterative retrieval system. Our framework uses three components: an initial retriever <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> that uses only the query, an iterative retriever <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> that conditions on both the query and previously retrieved documents, and a verifier model <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>. Our subsequent retriever <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> can be viewed as a version of task-aware retrieval with instruction <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Asai et al., 2022</a>)</cite> which is trained to retrieve documents closer to the query <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> but distinct from documents in the input (<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bigoplus_{d\in D_{\text{ctx}}}d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>⨁</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mtext>ctx</mtext></msub></mrow></msub><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bigoplus_{d\in D_{\text{ctx}}}d</annotation></semantics></math>). The initial and subsequent retrievers can be the same or different retrieval models, and we evaluate both possibilities in our experiments.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Initial Retriever</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The initial retriever produces a ranked list of <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> documents (<math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}=f_{i}(q,\mathcal{C},K)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}=f_{i}(q,\mathcal{C},K)</annotation></semantics></math>, line 2).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Verifier</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Retrieval is often noisy, and contains irrelevant documents.
Thus, we implement a verifier <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> that examines retrieval outputs and produces a verified subset <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{V}=\{d\in D_{i}:g(d,q)\wedge\text{rank}(d)\leq B\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>V</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mtext>rank</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{V}=\{d\in D_{i}:g(d,q)\wedge\text{rank}(d)\leq B\}</annotation></semantics></math> containing documents deemed relevant by verifier <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> is the verifier budget (line 4).</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The verified subset, <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>V</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{V}</annotation></semantics></math>, will constitute the final output (line 10) and will be used in forming a query for the next stage retrieval. For subsequent retrieval turns, we select the top <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> documents from the verified set (line 6) to form the concatenated query <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{r}=[q;\bigoplus_{d\in D_{\text{ctx}}}d]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo rspace="0em">;</mo><mrow><msub><mo>⨁</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mtext>ctx</mtext></msub></mrow></msub><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{r}=[q;\bigoplus_{d\in D_{\text{ctx}}}d]</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Subsequent Retriever</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Using this query, the subsequent retriever produces new output <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}=f_{r}(q_{r},\mathcal{C},B)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}=f_{r}(q_{r},\mathcal{C},B)</annotation></semantics></math> (line 8). Using augmented query <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> allows <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> to reason about which relevant documents remain unretrieved, promoting answer coverage across iterations.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Output</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To form the final output set, we accumulate verified documents across all rounds and add any remaining documents from the final iteration. Set semantics remove duplicates <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\text{out}}=\operatorname{TopK}(K,\Big(\bigcup_{t=0}^{T-1}D_{V}^{(t)}\Big)\;\cup\;D_{i}^{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>TopK</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo lspace="0em">⋃</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>V</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em" rspace="0.280em">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.502em">∪</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>T</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\text{out}}=\operatorname{TopK}(K,\Big(\bigcup_{t=0}^{T-1}D_{V}^{(t)}\Big)\;\cup\;D_{i}^{T})</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{V}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>V</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{V}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the verified set at round <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, and we take only the top <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K-|D_{\text{out}}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K-|D_{\text{out}}|</annotation></semantics></math> documents from the final retrieval <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}^{(T)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}^{(T)}</annotation></semantics></math> to ensure the total output size is <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Training</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we describe the training of two sets of retrievers <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>. We assume a training data, where each instance contains a query <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> paired with a set of gold documents <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>D</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> from corpus <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math>. We do not train the verifier, and use off-the-shelf LLMs. Our novelty lies in training the retriever <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> with the proposed iterative inference scenario. We thus generate training data (positive and negative target documents) from this inference scenario. Besides that, we use standard contrastive retriever learning objective <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Izacard et al., 2022</a>)</cite>:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L_{\theta}}=-\log\frac{\exp(s(f_{\theta}(x),f_{\theta}(d^{+}))/\tau)}{\sum_{d^{\in}D_{batch}}\exp(s(f_{\theta}(x),f_{\theta}(d))/\tau)}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L_{\theta}}=-\log\frac{\exp(s(f_{\theta}(x),f_{\theta}(d^{+}))/\tau)}{\sum_{d^{\in}D_{batch}}\exp(s(f_{\theta}(x),f_{\theta}(d))/\tau)}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where retriever <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> encodes the input query <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, positive document <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>, and in-batch documents <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> is a similarity function between the two embeddings, and <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is a temperature hyperparameter. We describe the process of constructing training data <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,d^{+},D_{batch})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,d^{+},D_{batch})</annotation></semantics></math> below.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training Data for Initial Retriever (<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>)</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each query <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> is paired with one positive document <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> and a set of negative documents <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{-}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We also randomly sample one negative document <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{-}</annotation></semantics></math> from the corpus <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math>. Additionally, we leverage in-batch negatives <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karpukhin et al., 2020</a>)</cite> such that all the other positive and negative documents from other training examples in the same batch serve as additional negatives. Thus, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{batch}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{batch}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes all the documents in the batch, including the positive document, the sampled negative, and the in-batch negatives. We use the input query <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> as is as <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, forming (<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,d^{+},D_{batch}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x,d^{+},D_{batch}</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training Data for Subsequent Retriever (<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>)</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As discussed in Section <a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 Iterative Retrieval Framework ‣ 3 Method ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> also takes gold documents as input in addition to query <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>, where the number of appended gold documents is controlled by hyperparameter <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. We first uniformly sample an integer <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m\in\{0,...,\min(M,|D^{*}|)\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m\in\{0,...,\min(M,|D^{*}|)\}</annotation></semantics></math>, and then sample <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> documents from our ground truth set <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>D</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> to form context <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\text{ctx}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mtext>ctx</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\text{ctx}}</annotation></semantics></math>. The input query <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> will be <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[q;D_{\text{ctx}}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mtext>ctx</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[q;D_{\text{ctx}}]</annotation></semantics></math>. The positive document <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> is randomly selected from the <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D^{*}\setminus D_{\text{ctx}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>D</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∖</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mtext>ctx</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D^{*}\setminus D_{\text{ctx}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Same as the training data for initial retriever, we randomly sample one negative document <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{-}</annotation></semantics></math> from the corpus <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math>, and leverage in-batch negatives.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Implementation Details</h3>

<section id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Retriever</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For all experiments, we initialize the retrievers with pre-trained, off-the-shelf dual encoder retrievers: Contriever-MSMARCO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Izacard et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and INF-Retriever-v1-1.5B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We use instances from the training portion of the QAMPARI dataset. Every model is fine-tuned for <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50</annotation></semantics></math>k steps. We use a learning rate of <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>, temperature <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=0.05</annotation></semantics></math>, batch size 48 per GPU, gradient accumulation of 2 steps, warm-up for 1K steps, and the AdamW optimizer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Loshchilov and Hutter, 2019</a>)</cite>. We use in-batch negatives and sample one negative document from the corpus. All experiments are conducted on NVIDIA H200 and L40 GPUs.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Verifier</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We prompt an LLM (Qwen <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Team, 2025</a>)</cite>)<span id="footnote1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">1</span>
                
                
                
                
                
                
                
              <span id="footnote1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507</span></span></span></span> to serve as a verifier. Given an input document <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> and a query <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>, the verifier outputs a binary label whether <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> is relevant to the query <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>. Formally, <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(d,q)=\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(d,q)=\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math>. We use vLLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kwon et al., 2023</a>)</cite> for inference. See Appendix <a href="#A3.SS1" title="C.1 Prompt for Qwen3 Verifier ‣ Appendix C Prompts &amp; Trajectories ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.1</span></a> for the prompt, and we discuss verifier performance in Section <a href="#S6.SS1" title="6.1 The Impact of Verifier Performance ‣ 6 Analysis ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S3.T1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 1</span>: </span><span id="S3.T1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Main Experimental Results on QAMPARI test set (N=1000). We report MRecall@100 and Recall@100. Our proposed methods outperform both the base retrievers (Base) and retrievers fine-tuned in-domain (FT (<math id="S3.T1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>)). RVR approaches also achieve much higher performance than agentic baselines. For our results, statistical significance is tested using bootstrap resampling with 10,000 trials at <math id="S3.T1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.05</annotation></semantics></math>. <math id="S3.T1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dagger" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>†</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dagger</annotation></semantics></math> indicates statistically significant improvement over FT<math id="S3.T1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(D_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(D_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>. * indicates statistically significant improvement over FT<math id="S3.T1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(D_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(D_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> + FT<math id="S3.T1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(D_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(D_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></figcaption>

</tbody>

</figure>
