<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experimental Settings</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Dataset</h3>

<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">QAMPARI</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">consists of open-domain questions paired with multiple valid answer strings (one example instance is shown in Fig <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). On average, each query is annotated with a set of <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16.58" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16.58</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16.58</annotation></semantics></math> gold documents and contains <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14.43" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>14.43</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14.43</annotation></semantics></math> unique valid answers. Unlike most other datasets such as HotpotQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2018</a>)</cite> and BrowseCompPlus <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> which assume one gold answer, this dataset allows studying multi-answer coverage. We use their original split (training, evaluation).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">QUEST</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">consists of queries paired with multiple valid answers, where each answer corresponds to a relevant Wikipedia document. The queries in QUEST specify set operations such as intersection, union, and difference (e.g., “what are some Films about bats that are not Superhero films” (difference), “films that are South Korean adventure comedies or Canadian fantasy comedies” (union)). The answer set size is 10.5 per query on average.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">WebQuestionsSP</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">consists of questions from the Google Suggest API with their semantic parses and corresponding answer entities in Freebase. We treat WebQuestionsSP as a multi-answer retrieval task as there are on average <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8.75</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.75</annotation></semantics></math> answers per query.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Retrieval Corpus</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For all datasets, we follow <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Amouyal et al. (2023)</a></cite> and use a Wikipedia dump from 2021-08-01 consisting of 25.9 million passages, averaging 100 words. See Appendix <a href="#A1.SS1" title="A.1 QAMPARI ‣ Appendix A Datasets ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.1</span></a>,  <a href="#A1.SS2" title="A.2 QUEST ‣ Appendix A Datasets ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a>, and  <a href="#A1.SS3" title="A.3 WebQuestionsSP ‣ Appendix A Datasets ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.3</span></a> for full data statistics.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Comparison Systems</h3>

<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Base <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{i}</annotation></semantics></math></h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate three pre-trained off-the-shelf retrieval models without fine-tuning.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">FT (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>)</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each pre-trained retriever is fine-tuned on the QAMPARI training dataset with standard contrastive objective (initial retriever setting in Section <a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Training ‣ 3 Method ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Agentic Retrievers</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We implement two strong open-source agentic baselines, Tongyi DeepResearch agent<span id="footnote2" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">2</span>
                
                
                
                
                
                
                
              <span id="footnote2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Alibaba-NLP/Tongyi-DeepResearch-30B-A3B</span></span></span></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Team et al., 2025</a>)</cite> and SearchR1<span id="footnote3" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">3</span>
                
                
                
                
                
                
                
              <span id="footnote3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">PeterJinGo/SearchR1-nq_hotpotqa_train-</span> <span id="footnote3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">qwen2.5-7b-em-ppo</span></span></span></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jin et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Both approaches use fixed retriever and train a LLM that generates search query. The former is continued pre-trained on agentic trajectories and post-trained on synthetic QA pairs. The latter is trained using PPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Schulman et al., 2017</a>)</cite> on Natural Questions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kwiatkowski et al., 2019</a>)</cite> and HotpotQA to maximize answer accuracy.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We use their trained model as is and follow their original implementations to retrieve <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> = 5 documents for Tongyi and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> = 3 documents for SearchR1, respectively. To obtain the final candidate document set, we combine the documents returned for each retriever call without duplicates. For each agent, we run until it outputs an answer or it has collected over <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> = 100 documents in total. If the agent has only collected <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> documents (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{a}&lt;K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{a}&lt;K</annotation></semantics></math>) upon termination, we additionally retrieve a set of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(K-K_{a})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(K-K_{a})</annotation></semantics></math> documents using the last query issued to the retriever and append them to the candidate document list.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The exact prompts we use are provided in Appendix <a href="#A3.SS2" title="C.2 Prompt for SearchR1 ‣ Appendix C Prompts &amp; Trajectories ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a> and <a href="#A3.SS3" title="C.3 Prompt for Tongyi ‣ Appendix C Prompts &amp; Trajectories ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a>, and example trajectory traces are provided in Appendix <a href="#A3.SS4" title="C.4 Trajectory for SearchR1 ‣ Appendix C Prompts &amp; Trajectories ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.4</span></a> and <a href="#A3.SS5" title="C.5 Trajectory for Tongyi ‣ Appendix C Prompts &amp; Trajectories ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.5</span></a>. We experiment them with two retriever configurations, base retriever and fine-tuned retriever for fair comparison.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the following hyperparameters for our approach: <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> = 2 retrieval rounds, verifier budget <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> = 100, context budget <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> = 3 for Contriever-MSMARCO and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> = 6 for INF-Retriever and Qwen3-Embedding. We evaluate three RVR configurations, differing in what is used for initial retriever (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>) and subsequent retriever (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>) : (1) FT (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>) + FT (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>): uses the same fine-tuned initial retriever <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> in both rounds; (2) FT (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> + <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>) + FT (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> + <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>): uses a single model trained on the union of two retrieval training data (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>); (3) Fine-tuned (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>) + Fine-tuned (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>) : uses fine-tuned <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> in round 1 and fine-tuned subsequent retriever <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> in round 2. This is more costly as it requires two retrieval indexes and two retrieval models.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Results</h2>

<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>In-Domain Results</h3>

<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Task Performance</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ Verifier ‣ 3.4 Implementation Details ‣ 3 Method ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> reports retrieval performance on the QAMPARI test set. Fine-tuning with in-domain data improves raw performance significantly, especially improving weaker base retrievers (Contriever, Qwen) to be on-par with stronger base model (INF-Retriever). In-domain retrievers improve the agentic approaches, but overall, the agentic approaches underperform the baseline in all three base models, even when paired with the fine-tuned retriever. This could be caused by distribution shift from their query LLM training data, which typically requires multi-hop reasoning but not comprehensive answer coverage.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T4" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 4</span>: </span><span id="S5.T4.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Out-of-Domain Generalization.<span id="S5.T4.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Results on QUEST (N=1727) and WebQuestionsSP (N=1639) test sets. We report MRecall@100 (MR) and Recall@100 (R). We report performances of different base retrieval models, agentic baselines, and RVR methods. For RVR, we use a verifier budget of 100. For our results, statistical significance is tested using bootstrap resampling with 10,000 trials at <math id="S5.T4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.05</annotation></semantics></math>. <math id="S5.T4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dagger" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>†</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dagger</annotation></semantics></math> indicates statistically significant improvement over Base. * indicates statistically significant improvement over Base + Base</span></span></figcaption>

</figure>
<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Our approach outperforms all baselines, raising both MRecall and R for all three base retrieval setting. Even using the same fine-tuned retriever <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> as the baseline, verification step can bring gains when paired with stronger base retrievers (Qwen3, INF). Training retriever to collect complementary output <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> further improves result. Having separate models (Fine-tuned <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(D_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(D_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> + Fine-tuned <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(D_{r})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(D_{r})</annotation></semantics></math>) further shows improvements.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Efficiency</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate the efficiency on the QAMPARI test set across two dimensions: time and memory. For time, we report seconds per query (s/q) for both retrieval and verification/query generation components, measured with NVIDIA H200 GPUs. Retrieval time includes query encoding and k-nearest-neighbor search over the document index. Verification time depends on the verifier budget <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> (number of documents verified per query) for our system, and the agentic search query generation process for agentic model. For memory, we report GPU memory usage in gigabytes for three components: the LLM verifier, the retrieval model, and the retrieval index.
Table <a href="#S3.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Verifier ‣ 3.4 Implementation Details ‣ 3 Method ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> reports the time efficiency across different retrieval models and configurations. The default single-pass outperforms others, while the agentic search is substantially slower. Two-round retrieval with verification incurs additional overhead that scales with the verifier budget and number of calls, making it 2-3 times slower than baseline.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S3.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ Verifier ‣ 3.4 Implementation Details ‣ 3 Method ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> shows memory requirements, reporting both RVR and agentic search requires additional GPU memory compared to baseline. Having a separate model for initial retriever and subsequent retriever is more costly.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Generalization to Other Datasets</h3>

<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Setting</h4>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate our models on two out-of-domain datasets: QUEST and WebQuestionsSP. We find that fine-tuned <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> underperforms the baseline on these datasets, potentially due to domain shift. Therefore, we use the base retriever for the initial retrieval in our RVR framework. We evaluate two settings: (1) using the off-the-shelf retriever for both initial and subsequent retrieval (Base + Base), and (2) using the base retriever for initial retrieval and a subsequent retriever <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> finetuned on QAMPARI (Base + FT(<math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>)).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Results</h4>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ Task Performance ‣ 5.1 In-Domain Results ‣ 5 Results ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> reports results with <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>=100, while Table <a href="#A2.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ B.2 Impact of Varying Input Documents on MRecall@K ‣ Appendix B More Analysis ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> in the Appendix shows results with <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>=50. Our RVR framework largely outperforms the one-round baseline across both datasets. For QUEST, Base + FT(<math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>) achieves the strongest performance, demonstrating that a retriever trained to find complementary results generalizes well despite being fine-tuned on QAMPARI. For WebQuestionsSP, RVR still outperforms the baseline, though Base + FT(<math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>) performs slightly worse than Base + Base due to domain mismatch between QAMPARI and WebQuestionsSP.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Analysis</h2>

<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>The Impact of Verifier Performance</h3>

<section id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Intrinsic Verifier Evaluation</h4>

<div id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The goal of verifier is to identify retrieved documents that are relevant to the original query. To evaluate their performance, we generate the following data: for each query in QAMPARI test set, we use three fine-tuned retrieval models <math id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> from different base retrievers to retrieve 100 documents. We judge whether they contain gold answer using the gold label set. For this set, we observe 21.07% being positive and 78.93% being negative documents.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We report the performance of three LLMs, GPT-5-nano, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Team, 2025</a>)</cite>, and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Team, 2025</a>)</cite>, as verifier on this dataset. Table <a href="#S6.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ Intrinsic Verifier Evaluation ‣ 6.1 The Impact of Verifier Performance ‣ 6 Analysis ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> presents the results. Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 model achieves the highest recall, which aligns with our objective of maximizing retrieval coverage. Therefore, we use this as the verifier for main experiments.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T5" class="ltx_table">

</section>
<section id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Extrinsic Verifier Evaluation</h4>

<div id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we isolate the impact of verifier performance in end-to-end retrieval performance. We evaluate verifier performance by comparing against a baseline and an upper bound. As a baseline (TopK), we use the top <math id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> documents ranked by the initial retriever to form the query context without a verifier. The final output set (K=100) combines the top 50 documents from the initial retriever with the top 50 non-duplicate documents from the subsequent retriever.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.F2" class="ltx_figure">
<p id="S6.F2.3" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center ltx_align_center"><span id="S6.F2.3.1" class="ltx_text"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18425v1/varying_iterations.svg" id="S6.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/165;" width="476" height="165"></object></span></p>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S6.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S6.F2.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Multi-turn Generalization Results. This figure illustrates the change in Recall@100 and MRecall@100 across five iterations with a verifier budget of 100. Left panels show results with LLM verifier (Qwen3-30B), while right panels show results with oracle verifier that selects documents containing unique answer strings to be used as input. Performance with the LLM verifier plateaus after the second iteration, whereas the oracle verifier shows continued improvement, indicating substantial headroom for better verification mechanisms.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As an upper bound, we use oracle verifier that has access to gold answer strings. For each example, we have a set of answer strings. Our oracle verifier leverages these answer strings to determine which documents are gold. If a document contains any of the answer strings, it is considered a gold document.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S6.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ Intrinsic Verifier Evaluation ‣ 6.1 The Impact of Verifier Performance ‣ 6 Analysis ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> presents the comparison across verifier settings: oracle, LLM (Qwen3-30B), and TopK. Across all base models, we see noticeable gains with oracle verifier, suggesting performance gain can be achieved by improving the verifier.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Multi-turn Generalization</h3>

<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S6.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ Extrinsic Verifier Evaluation ‣ 6.1 The Impact of Verifier Performance ‣ 6 Analysis ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> compares performance across five iterations using both LLM and oracle verifiers. The left panel shows results with our LLM verifier (Qwen3-30B), where gains plateau after the second iteration. The right panel shows results with an oracle verifier that selects documents containing unique answer strings for <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\text{ctx}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mtext>ctx</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\text{ctx}}</annotation></semantics></math>, demonstrating steady improvements across all five iterations. This disparity suggests the LLM verifier tends to select redundant documents in later iterations, even when the retrieved set contains documents with unique answers. These results indicate that improved verification mechanisms could substantially enhance RVR performance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.3 </span>The Impact of Verifier Budget</h3>

<div id="S6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S6.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 6.3 The Impact of Verifier Budget ‣ 6 Analysis ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> plots the system performance for varying verifier budget (10, 20, 50, 100 documents) to evaluate models under more resource-constrained settings. The scores for 100 document setting is the same as reported in Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ Verifier ‣ 3.4 Implementation Details ‣ 3 Method ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We compare two settings of our Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve, one with FT(<math id="S6.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>) and another with FT(<math id="S6.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>) and FT(<math id="S6.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>). Across all models, the absolute performance decreases as the verifier budget shrinks. Using fine-tuned subsequent retriever FT(<math id="S6.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>) was particularly helpful in more restrictive budget setting.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.F3" class="ltx_figure">
<p id="S6.F3.3" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center ltx_align_center"><span id="S6.F3.3.1" class="ltx_text"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18425v1/varying_verifier_budget.svg" id="S6.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/166;" width="476" height="166"></object></span></p>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S6.F3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="S6.F3.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Varying the verifier budget. We evaluate MR@100 across three new verifier budgets on QAMPARI dataset. RVR is shown in green and blue, while our one-round baseline in red. See Appendix <a href="#A2.SS1" title="B.1 Impact of Verifier Budget on Recall@K ‣ Appendix B More Analysis ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a> for Recall@100 results.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.4 </span>The Impact of Varying Input Length</h3>

<figure id="S6.F4" class="ltx_figure">
<p id="S6.F4.3" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center ltx_align_center"><span id="S6.F4.3.1" class="ltx_text"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18425v1/vary_input_precision_mrecall.svg" id="S6.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:333/237;" width="333" height="237"></object></span></p>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S6.F4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="S6.F4.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">The performance (MRecall@100) with varying number of input documents at inference time (Context Budget <math id="S6.F4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>). We compare models fine-tuned with different maximum document counts (3, 6, and 12 docs) for INF and Qwen3. Different colors denote fine-tuning with different number of documents, and shapes indicate the retrievers used. Other metric results (Recall@100) are provided in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS2" title="B.2 Impact of Varying Input Documents on MRecall@K ‣ Appendix B More Analysis ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>. </span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We study the impact of varying the maximum number of input documents provided to the subsequent retriever. Here, we do not report results for Contriever, as it has a sequence length limit of 512 tokens, resulting in truncation when we provide more than <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> input documents. We run inference with our RVR model (Fine-tuned + Ours) setting, fine-tuned with a maximum of 3, 6, and 12 input documents. We further vary the context budget, <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, used during inference time.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A2.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ B.2 Impact of Varying Input Documents on MRecall@K ‣ Appendix B More Analysis ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> displays the trends, as we sample from 0 up to 12 input documents. We find that increasing the number of documents at inference time beyond 6 does not show strong gains. We also observe that on average, models fine-tuned with up to <math id="S6.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math> input documents perform better.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.5 </span>Ablation Studies on Retrievers</h3>

<div id="S6.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S6.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ 6.5 Ablation Studies on Retrievers ‣ 6 Analysis ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> presents ablation study of retriever components. In rows 1 and 2, we report using off-the-shelf base retriever instead of fine-tuned retriever for <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>. As long as we fine-tune the subsequent retriever, the performance is quite competitive, sometimes even outperforming setting with both initial and subsequent retriever fine-tuned.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T7" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S6.T7.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 7</span>: </span><span id="S6.T7.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Ablation study on QAMPARI test set. <section id="S6.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.6 </span>The contribution of 1st turn vs. 2nd turn retrieval</h3>

<div id="S6.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We analyze the individual contributions of our first-stage (base) and second-stage (iterative) retrievers. Table <a href="#S6.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ 6.6 The contribution of 1st turn vs. 2nd turn retrieval ‣ 6 Analysis ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> presents a breakdown across our three models with <math id="S6.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>=100. Table <a href="#A2.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ B.2 Impact of Varying Input Documents on MRecall@K ‣ Appendix B More Analysis ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> shows results for <math id="S6.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>=50.</p>
</div>

<td id="S6.T8.5.11.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S6.T8.5.11.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">55.32</span></td>
<td id="S6.T8.5.11.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_r" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S6.T8.5.11.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">26.12</span></td>
<td id="S6.T8.5.11.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S6.T8.5.11.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">7.50</span></td>
<td id="S6.T8.5.11.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S6.T8.5.11.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">0.72</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The first-stage retriever provides the initial set of relevant documents. Across all models, the first stage contributes approximately 50 gold documents, corresponding to 7 unique answers, per question on average, demonstrating that initial retriever already captures a substantial portion of relevant information. The second-stage iterative retriever, conditioned on verified documents from the first stage, contributes an additional 22-26 gold documents, up to 1 unique answer, per question. This consistent improvement demonstrates that conditioning on previously retrieved context enables the model to discover initially missed documents.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduced Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve framework, a framework that conditions on previously retrieved evidence and explicitly optimizes for answer coverage. By training retrievers to predict missing gold documents and integrating verifier-guided iteration, our approach consistently expands retrieval coverage while reducing redundancy. Results on QAMPARI and zero-shot generalization to QUEST demonstrate that iterative conditioning provides a robust and general mechanism for improving retrieval completeness.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Impact Statement</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper introduces a retrieval framework designed to improve answer coverage and reduce redundancy in information retrieval systems. By enabling retrieval models to iteratively reason over previously retrieved evidence, the proposed approach may improve the completeness and reliability of systems used in applications such as search engines, question answering, and knowledge discovery.</p>
</div>
<div id="Sx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Potential positive impacts include more thorough information access, reduced bias toward dominant viewpoints, and improved support for users seeking comprehensive answers. As with any retrieval technology, the quality of results ultimately depend on the underlying data sources and the design of downstream systems. Potential risks mirror those of existing retrieval systems, including surfacing misinformation or amplifying biases present in the corpus.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>QAMPARI</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A1.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ A.3 WebQuestionsSP ‣ Appendix A Datasets ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> displays our dataset statistics in detail. An example of a gold document from our QAMPARI test set, along with the query and answer strings is below.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Query</span>: What manga was drawn by Ryoichi Ikegami?</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Answer Strings</span>: Heat, <span id="A1.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Mai, the Psychic Girl</span>, Wounded Man, Sanctuary, Crying Freeman, Strain</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Document Text</span>: <span id="A1.SS1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Mai, the Psychic Girl</span>, known simply as in Japan, is a manga written by Kazuya Kudo and illustrated by Ryoichi Ikegami. The main character is Mai Kuju, a 14-year-old Japanese girl with powerful psychic abilities. She is being pursued by the Wisdom Alliance, an organization which secretly strives to control the world. The alliance already controls four other powerful psychic children, and it has hired the Kaieda Intelligence Agency to capture Mai. Media. Manga. <span id="A1.SS1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Mai, the Psychic Girl</span> is one of the first manga series to be fully published in English.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>QUEST</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Below, we show an example query from the QUEST test set, its associated answer string, and a document from our corpus that contains this answer. Table <a href="#A1.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ A.3 WebQuestionsSP ‣ Appendix A Datasets ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> shows additional dataset statistics.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Query</span>: what are some 1950s comedy mystery or spy comedy films</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Answer Strings</span>: The Hole (1957 film), Charade (1953 film), Hot Stuff (1956 film), The Trouble with Harry, Father Brown (film), The Runaway Bus, Boston Quackie, <span id="A1.SS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">My Favorite Spy</span>, The Fuller Brush Girl, Scared Stiff (1953 film), Our Man in Havana (film), Spy Chasers, Mrs. O’Malley and Mr. Malone, Clipped Wings (1953 film), Commotion on the Ocean, Down Among the Z Men, Knock on Wood (film), Top Secret (1952 film)</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Document Text</span>:
<span id="A1.SS2.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">My Favorite Spy</span> is a 1951 comedy film directed by Norman Z. McLeod and starring Bob Hope and Hedy Lamarr. Plot. US intelligence agents recruit burlesque comic Peanuts White to pose as international spy Eric Augustine, whom he resembles, to acquire a million-dollar microfilm in Tangier. There, he encounters the irresistible Lily Dalbray, Augustine’s one-time friend, who is now in league with his arch-enemy, Brubaker.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>WebQuestionsSP</h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Below, we show an example query from the WebQuestionsSP test set, its associated answer string, and a document from our corpus that contains this answer. Table <a href="#A1.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ A.3 WebQuestionsSP ‣ Appendix A Datasets ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> shows additional dataset statistics.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Query</span>: what does jamaican people speak</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Answer Strings</span>: <span id="A1.SS3.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Jamaican English</span>, Jamaican Creole English Language</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Document Text</span>: In <span id="A1.SS3.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Jamaican English</span>, normally reduced English vowels are sometimes not reduced, and other times are hyper-reduced, so that ẗokenïs not but, yet c̈ementc̈an be as reduced as; the exact nuances of the rules at play here are also highly debated. Language use: Jamaican Standard English versus Patois. Jamaican Standard English and Jamaican Patois exist together in a post-creole speech continuum. Jamaican (Creole/Patois) is used by most people for everyday, informal situations - it is the language most Jamaicans use at home and are most familiar with, as well as the language of most local popular music.</p>
</div>

<section id="A1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.4 </span>Instruction Used for Instruction Tuned Models</h3>

<div id="A1.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the same instruction to finetune our Qwen3-0.6B-Embed and inf-retriever-1.5B models: <span id="A1.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Given a query, retrieve relevant passages that answer the query</span>. We use this instruction during both fine-tuning and inference.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>More Analysis</h2>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Impact of Verifier Budget on Recall@K</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A2.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ B.2 Impact of Varying Input Documents on MRecall@K ‣ Appendix B More Analysis ‣ RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> displays Precision@100 and Recall@100 with verifier budgets of 10, 20, 50, and 100.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Impact of Varying Input Documents on MRecall@K</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
